integrity: Each cycle-leaf pair has weight at least two, with equality only in state (0,2). Three consecutive baseline pairs are impossible because the middle zero cycle vertex would have closed-neighborhood weight two. Hitting every cyclic three-block therefore requires at least ceil(n/3) exceptional pairs. A binary cycle construction with ceil(n/3) ones and all leaves labeled two attains the bound.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is for sunlet graphs C_n corona K_1 with n at least three, not arbitrary coronas or nonuniform pendant cycles.
The 2024 invariant also called perfect Roman {3}-domination has a different definition and is not covered by this theorem.
Exhaustive full-label computation covers n=3,4,5; larger checks use a cycle-state minimization and direct construction verification.
A differently phrased or non-indexed treatment of the same sunlet family may exist.
title: Perfect double Italian domination of sunlet graphs
